title: MongoDB Setup & Connection

introduction.heading: MongoDB Setup, Configuration & Troubleshooting
introduction.description: A comprehensive guide to setting up MongoDB Atlas, connecting from your Node.js application, configuring network access, and resolving common connection issues. Includes DNS fixes for connection errors and proper configuration for cloud deployments like Render.

prerequisites: MongoDB Atlas account (free tier available at mongodb.com)
Basic understanding of databases and connection strings

steps.title: Create MongoDB Atlas Account & Cluster
steps.description: Set up a free MongoDB Atlas account and create your first database cluster.
steps.note: Keep your database credentials secure! Store them in .env file, never in code.

steps.title: Configure Network Access (IP Whitelist)
steps.description: Add allowed IP addresses to MongoDB Atlas to enable connections from your application.
steps.note: For development use 'Allow Access from Anywhere' (0.0.0.0/0). For production, add specific IPs of your servers.

steps.title: Get Your Connection String
steps.description: Retrieve the MongoDB connection string from Atlas to use in your application.
steps.note: Never hardcode the connection string! Always use environment variables.

steps.title: Install MongoDB Connection Packages
steps.description: Install Mongoose (recommended ODM) for MongoDB connection and schema management.

subSteps.title: .env Configuration
subSteps.description: Create a .env file in your project root with MongoDB credentials.
subSteps.note: Add .env to your .gitignore file! Create .env.example with dummy values for documentation.

subSteps.title: Basic Connection Setup
subSteps.description: Connect to MongoDB in your main application file.

steps.title: Troubleshooting Connection Errors - DNS Fix
steps.description: Resolve 'ENOTFOUND' and DNS-related connection errors by configuring DNS servers.

subSteps.title: DNS Fix Implementation
subSteps.description: Configure DNS servers to resolve MongoDB connection issues.
subSteps.note: Place the DNS configuration BEFORE any other MongoDB or network operations. 1.1.1.1 is Cloudflare's DNS server.

subSteps.title: Why This Works
subSteps.description: Understanding the DNS fix for MongoDB connection issues.
subSteps.note: This fix is especially useful on shared hosting or cloud platforms like Render.

steps.title: MongoDB Atlas IP Whitelist for Render
steps.description: Configure MongoDB Atlas network access specifically for Render deployment.
steps.note: Render (and most other PaaS providers) uses dynamic outbound IPs, so pinning individual IPs isn't practical - add 0.0.0.0/0 to the IP Access List for that cluster instead.

steps.title: Define Mongoose Schemas & Models
steps.description: Create data schemas and models for your MongoDB collections.

steps.title: Basic CRUD Operations
steps.description: Create, Read, Update, and Delete documents in MongoDB using Mongoose.

steps.title: Query Operators & Filters
steps.description: Use MongoDB query operators to filter and find documents efficiently.
steps.note: Always use operators like $ne, $gt, etc. for queries. Avoid hardcoding field values in conditions.

steps.title: Connection Pooling & Best Practices
steps.description: Optimize MongoDB connections with proper pooling configuration and error handling.
steps.note: Proper pooling configuration improves performance, especially in production environments.

steps.title: Common Connection Errors & Solutions
steps.description: Troubleshoot and resolve common MongoDB connection issues.
steps.note: Most connection issues are related to network access, DNS, or incorrect credentials.
